expectedText:
DMV EMPLOYER PULL NOTICE PROGRAM — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme Corp.

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California's Department of Motor Vehicles (DMV) Employer Pull Notice (EPN) Program, a driving-record monitoring system established under Vehicle Code section 1808.1, in connection with Acme Corp.'s employment of Jordan Lee in the position of Delivery Driver with a start date of September 4, 2026. It summarizes selected requirements of that statute. It is not a substitute for Acme Corp.'s own enrollment paperwork with the DMV's Pull Notice Program, and it does not state whether Jordan Lee's particular position in fact falls within the statute's scope, which depends on the vehicle and license class or certificate the position requires.

WHAT THE PULL-NOTICE SYSTEM IS
California law defines a "pull-notice system" as a process for providing an enrolled employer with a report showing a covered driver's current public driving record as recorded by the department, plus any subsequent convictions, failures to appear, accidents, driver's license suspensions, driver's license revocations, or other actions taken against the driving privilege or certificate that are added to the driver's record while the employer's notification request remains active — without the employer having to separately request a new record each time. Participation means the employer obtains a requester code from the department and enrolls its covered drivers under that code.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The employer of a driver who drives a vehicle specified in subdivision (k) shall participate in a pull-notice system, which is a process for the purpose of providing the employer with a report showing the driver’s current public record as recorded by the department, and any subsequent convictions, failures to appear, accidents, driver’s license suspensions, driver’s license revocations, or any other actions taken against the driving privilege or certificate, added to the driver’s record while the employer’s notification request remains valid and uncanceled. As used in this section, participation in the pull-notice system means obtaining a requester code and enrolling all employed drivers who drive a vehicle specified in subdivision (k) under that requester code."
  — Cal. Veh. Code § 1808.1(b) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Vehicle Code, pull-notice system defined (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1808.1.&lawCode=VEH)
  Known gap: This clause quotes subdivision (b) of Vehicle Code section 1808.1 only. The pre-hire report duty (subdivision (a)) and the periodic-report duty (subdivision (c)) are separate obligations within the same section, covered in other clauses in this set rather than here. This clause does not cover the enrollment fee the department may charge (subdivision (h)), or the department's own procedures for issuing a requester code, which the statute does not itself spell out. Separately: the statute's text, as fetched and reviewed for this clause set, does not state that the employer must obtain the employee's consent, or give the employee notice, before enrolling them in the pull-notice system or before obtaining the driving-record reports described in this and the related clauses below. That absence is reported as a research finding about the text of this one statute, not as a conclusion that no consent or notice obligation exists anywhere in California or federal law (for example, under general privacy statutes) — that broader question was not researched for this clause set.

WHICH VEHICLES TRIGGER THE PARTICIPATION REQUIREMENT
The pull-notice participation duty applies only to the employer of a driver who operates a vehicle for which the driver is required to hold a class A or class B driver's license, a class C license with certain endorsements, or one of several specified certificates, or who drives certain small passenger vehicles operated for compensation under a charter-party or passenger-stage authority or as a permitted taxicab. An employer whose employees do not drive a vehicle within this defined scope is not brought within the pull-notice requirement by this statute.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "This section applies to a vehicle for the operation of which the driver is required to have a class A or class B driver’s license, a class C license with any endorsement issued pursuant to Section 15278, a class C license issued pursuant to Section 12814.7, or a certificate issued pursuant to Section 12517, 12519, 12520, 12523, 12523.5, or 12527, a passenger vehicle having a seating capacity of not more than 10 persons, including the driver, operated for compensation by a charter-party carrier of passengers or passenger stage corporation pursuant to a certificate of public convenience and necessity or a permit issued by the Public Utilities Commission, or a permitted taxicab company as described in Section 53075.5 of the Government Code."
  — Cal. Veh. Code § 1808.1(k) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Vehicle Code, vehicles and license classes within scope (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1808.1.&lawCode=VEH)
  Known gap: This clause quotes subdivision (k) of Vehicle Code section 1808.1 only, which defines scope by cross-referencing several other Vehicle Code license and certificate provisions (Sections 15278, 12814.7, 12517, 12519, 12520, 12523, 12523.5, 12527, and 53075.5 of the Government Code); those cross-referenced sections were not independently fetched or verified for this clause set, so this clause states the scope in the general terms subdivision (k) itself uses rather than reciting the detail of each cross-referenced license or certificate type. It also does not cover subdivision (j)'s narrower rule for a "casual driver" (one employed less than 30 days in the preceding six months), or subdivision (m)'s extension of the same obligations to a motor carrier that contracts with a person to drive a covered vehicle it owns or leases. Genuine correction to this brief's premise: Vehicle Code section 12804.6 was fetched and reviewed, and it does connect to the pull-notice system — it provides that a transit busdriver's certificate status becomes part of the pull-notice and periodic reports issued under this section — but it does not itself impose a separate employer mandatory-enrollment duty; it is not cited here because it does not independently expand who must enroll. Vehicle Code section 13369 was also fetched and reviewed, and it is not an enrollment-trigger statute at all: it sets the department's own criteria for refusing, suspending, or revoking specified driver certificates and endorsements (passenger transportation, hazardous materials, schoolbus, and similar categories) based on a driving record; it does not impose or expand any employer pull-notice enrollment obligation, so it is omitted from this clause set as not actually on point.

PRE-HIRE DRIVING RECORD REPORT
Before employing a driver to operate a vehicle within the program's scope, a prospective employer must obtain a report showing that driver's current public driving record as recorded by the department. A report is treated as current only if it was issued less than 30 days before the date the employer employs the driver.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The prospective employer of a driver who drives a vehicle specified in subdivision (k) shall obtain a report showing the driver’s current public record as recorded by the department. For purposes of this subdivision, a report is current if it was issued less than 30 days before the date the employer employs the driver."
  — Cal. Veh. Code § 1808.1(a) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Vehicle Code, pre-hire driving record report (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1808.1.&lawCode=VEH)
  Known gap: This clause quotes subdivision (a) of Vehicle Code section 1808.1 only. It does not cover that same subdivision's further requirements that the report be reviewed, signed, and dated by the employer, maintained at the employer's place of business until the pull-notice report described elsewhere in the section is received, and presented on request to an authorized California Highway Patrol representative — those requirements exist in the statute but are not quoted here. It also does not cover the different, longer six-month currency period that subdivision (j) sets for a "casual driver."

PERIODIC DRIVING RECORD REPORT
Beyond the pre-hire report, an employer of a driver who operates a vehicle within the program's scope must obtain a periodic report from the department at least every 12 months, and must use it to verify that the employee's driver's license has not been suspended or revoked, the employee's traffic-violation point count, and whether the employee has been convicted of a violation of Vehicle Code section 23152 or 23153 (driving under the influence).

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "The employer of a driver of a vehicle specified in subdivision (k) shall, additionally, obtain a periodic report from the department at least every 12 months. The employer shall verify that each employee’s driver’s license has not been suspended or revoked, the employee’s traffic violation point count, and whether the employee has been convicted of a violation of Section 23152 or 23153."
  — Cal. Veh. Code § 1808.1(c) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Vehicle Code, periodic driving record report (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1808.1.&lawCode=VEH)
  Known gap: This clause quotes subdivision (c) of Vehicle Code section 1808.1 only. It does not cover that same subdivision's further requirements that the report be signed and dated by the employer, maintained at the employer's principal place of business, and presented on demand to an authorized California Highway Patrol representative. It also does not cover subdivision (i), under which the department may, when feasible, establish an automatic mail or electronic delivery procedure for these periodic reports without the employer making individual requests.

DISCONTINUING ENROLLMENT WHEN EMPLOYMENT ENDS
When a driver's employment ends, the employer must notify the department to discontinue that driver's enrollment in the pull-notice system.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-04]
  "Upon the termination of a driver’s employment, the employer shall notify the department to discontinue the driver’s enrollment in the pull-notice system."
  — Cal. Veh. Code § 1808.1(d) (leginfo.legislature.ca.gov text), California Vehicle Code, discontinuing pull-notice enrollment (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?sectionNum=1808.1.&lawCode=VEH)
  Known gap: This clause quotes subdivision (d) of Vehicle Code section 1808.1 only, a single sentence that is the entirety of that subdivision. It does not address whether or how enrollment must be adjusted for reasons other than termination of employment altogether (for example, a driver's reassignment to a role that no longer involves operating a covered vehicle), which this subdivision does not itself speak to. It also does not describe the department's own procedure for processing a discontinuation notice, which the statute does not specify.

ACKNOWLEDGMENT
By signing below, the undersigned acknowledge that this information sheet was provided and that it states general rules of California law about the DMV Employer Pull Notice Program rather than advice about Jordan Lee's specific position or Acme Corp.'s specific legal obligations.

By: _______________
Date: _______________

Employee: Jordan Lee
Signature: _______________
Date: _______________
